messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

Memory:
- As of 2026-04-13, the Ember team still owns the reporting service. [valid 2026-04-13 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2026-04-13-2]
- On 2026-04-14 the Dune team noticed that the reporting service's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy and pinged the owners. [valid 2026-04-14 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2026-04-14-2]
- On 2026-05-28 the Ember team noticed that the ledger service's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy and pinged the owners. [valid 2026-05-28 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2026-05-28]
- On 2026-05-27 the Atlas team noticed that the indexer's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy and pinged the owners. [valid 2026-05-27 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-05-27]
- On 2025-11-03 the Boreal team noticed that the notification service's CPU sat at 90 percent after the traffic shift. [valid 2025-11-03 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-11-03-2]
- On 2026-04-08 the Atlas team noticed that webhooks' request volume halved following the client rollout and flagged it because it is not their service. [valid 2026-04-08 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-04-08]
- On 2026-04-16 the Atlas team noticed that the ledger service's disk usage jumped 30 percent following the retention change and flagged it because it is not their service. [valid 2026-04-16 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-04-16]
- The notifier relies on the bus for delivery events, so if the bus is down the notifier is down. [valid 2025-02-11 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-02-11]
- As of 2025-04-07, the Ember team reported that the notifier's request volume halved after the client rollout. [valid 2025-04-07 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2025-04-07]
- As of 2025-09-23, the reporting service no longer depends on the ledger service. [valid 2025-09-23 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2025-09-23]
- The notifier is owned by the Dune team as of 2025-06-27; the earlier handover note of 2025-06-11 saying Cinder took ownership was written against the wrong team, and Cinder never owned it. [valid 2025-06-27 to now; recorded by handover/2025-06-27-notifier-correction]
    earlier: The notifier is owned by Cinder as of 2025-06-11, having moved from the Boreal team. [valid 2025-06-11 to 2025-06-27; recorded by handover/2025-06-11-notifier]
    earlier: The Boreal team owns the notifier. [valid 2025-01-09 to 2025-06-11; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-01-09-2]
- On 2026-06-04 the Boreal team noticed that the product catalog's memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change and pinged the owners. [valid 2026-06-04 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2026-06-04]
- On 2026-05-22 the Dune team noticed that the auth gateway's CPU sat at 90 percent after the traffic shift and pinged the owners. [valid 2026-05-22 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2026-05-22-2]
- The notifier's flat one-second retry was hammering the push provider during its outages. [valid 2025-02-21 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-02-21]
- As of 2025-11-24, the Atlas team owns the bus, having taken it over from the Boreal team. [valid 2025-11-24 to now; recorded by handover/2025-11-24-event-bus]
    earlier: As of 2025-08-15, the Boreal team still owns the bus. [valid 2025-08-15 to 2025-11-24; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-08-15-2]
- As of 2026-02-11, the feature-flags service is owned by the Atlas team, having moved from the Ember team; the Dune team never owned it. [decision; valid 2026-03-09 to now; recorded by handover/2026-03-09-feature-flags-correction]
    earlier: As of 2026-02-11, the feature-flags service is owned by the Dune team, having moved from the Ember team. [decision; valid 2026-02-11 to 2026-03-09; recorded by handover/2026-02-11-feature-flags]
- On 2026-04-01, ownership of the indexer transferred from the Atlas team to the Boreal team. [valid 2026-04-01 to now; recorded by handover/2026-04-01-search-indexer]
- On 2025-12-31 the Atlas team noticed that the feature-flags service's queue depth hit 50,000 following the marketing send and flagged it because it is not their service. [valid 2025-12-31 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-12-31]
- The indexer was owned by the Atlas team from 2025-05-20, taking over from Cinder, until ownership transferred to the Boreal team on 2026-04-01. [decision; valid 2026-04-01 to now; recorded by handover/2026-04-01-search-indexer]
    earlier: The indexer is owned by the Atlas team as of 2025-05-20, taking over from Cinder. [decision; valid 2025-05-20 to 2026-04-01; recorded by handover/2025-05-20-search-indexer]
    earlier: The indexer is owned by Cinder. [valid 2025-01-17 to 2025-05-20; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-01-17-2]

Question: Which team owns the service that the notifier depends on?

message.reasoning: The notifier relies on the bus for delivery events. So the service the notifier depends on is the bus. Who owns the bus? As of 2025-11-24, the Atlas team owns the bus, having taken it over from the Boreal team. Valid to now. Today is 2026-06-30, so Atlas owns the bus.
